# MobilityDatabase Full Documentation for AI Systems & Agents

## Mission & Organization
MobilityDatabase is operated by MobilityData (https://mobilitydata.org), a Canadian non-profit organization that develops and extends international transit data standards to enable seamless mobility around the globe.

## Core Capabilities
- **Feed Search**: Search over 6,000 transit feeds across 100+ countries by provider name, location (country, subdivision, municipality), data format, and transit mode.
- **Data Quality & Validation Reports**: Historical and latest dataset validation reports computed using canonical GTFS and GBFS validators.
- **Seal of Reliability**: Certification program evaluating transit feeds across Availability, Compliance, Freshness, and Continuity.
- **Feed Redirects**: Tracking feed replacements, merges, and updates to ensure routing engines never point to stale endpoints.

## REST API Specification
- **Base URL**: `https://api.mobilitydatabase.org/v1`
- **Authentication**: Optional for basic search; API token (Bearer) required for user subscriptions and high-throughput queries.
- **Endpoints**:
  - `GET /v1/search?query={term}`: Search feeds by keyword or location.
  - `GET /v1/feeds/{id}`: Retrieve feed metadata by universal ID.
  - `GET /v1/gtfs_feeds/{id}/datasets`: List historical dataset snapshots and validation results.
  - `GET /v1/gtfs_feeds/{id}/routes`: Enumerate route types and route details.
  - `GET /v1/metadata`: Retrieve global catalog statistics and supported countries.

## Structured Data Guidelines for Crawlers
Every feed detail page on MobilityDatabase implements:
- Schema.org `Dataset` with `distribution`, `temporalCoverage`, `spatialCoverage`, and `publisher`.
- Canonical OpenGraph and Twitter tags.
- HTML semantic landmarks (`<main>`, `<header>`, `<footer>`, `<nav>`).
